rulings.item: R4 blind item 5(a): reader reads 沿袭海湾传统 as 'local tradition' and asks why imported timber
rulings.ruling: NOT A TRANSLATION DEFECT — stable reader inference from a true, sourced pairing the source itself states; consistent with the R3 zh judge.
rulings.reason: Across four rounds the tension decayed while the wording changed: R1 'local materials' vs imported = explicit contradiction (a real defect, fixed at source); R2/R3 'local tradition' vs imported = pause; R4 'Gulf tradition' vs imported = a 'why' question, no longer a contradiction. The Chinese lead-in is now exactly the source's (traditional Gulf manner), and ar/en readers meet the identical pairing: Gulf tradition + timber once imported to the Gulf. The gloss itself already says this imported timber was commonly used in Gulf traditional building, so tradition-with-imported-material is stated, not contradictory. Answering 'why imported' (timber scarcity, trade routes) would need causal facts the source does not state — the fact fence forbids adding them. Whatever any intro said, readers paired 'tradition' with 'imported'; that is the content, not the rendering. Chinese mirrors the source; no change.

rulings.item: R4 blind item 5(b): move the gloss out of the list — 「……屋顶以椰枣树干和尚达尔木杆铺成（尚达尔木是海湾传统建筑常用的进口木料）……」
rulings.ruling: REJECTED — not a warranted minimal change for this batch.
rulings.reason: (1) BRIEF round 4: the intro alone changes, the gloss stays in its approved R3 form. (2) The first-mention form 尚达尔木杆（chandal，海湾传统建筑常用的进口木料） is termbase-locked and shared with hubaish.md; restructuring it here breaks cross-page consistency and the one-position scope. (3) The suggested text drops 与石块 (stone) — an omission of a source fact (roofs of palm trunks, chandal wood and stone) — and drops the Latin chandal tag. (4) It would not answer (a): the content (tradition + imported) is identical. If the owner wants a lighter first-mention pattern, it belongs in a separate termbase batch (termbase.json + hubaish.md + qasr-ibrahim.md together).
